strengths: Well-designed dual-level architecture (patch + pixel) with thorough ablation studies demonstrating each component's contribution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (ImageNet 256×256 and 1024×1024, GenEval, DPG-Bench) with multiple model variants
Competitive FID score (1.61) for pixel-space diffusion while avoiding VAE bottlenecks of latent-space methods
Addresses a genuine limitation of latent-space diffusion with principled architectural design
Strong technical execution with clear presentation, detailed appendices, and reproducibility focus
Successfully demonstrates practical scalability to 1024×1024 resolution in pixel space
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - individual components (AdaLN, token compaction, dual-pathway) are relatively standard; contribution is primarily engineering combination rather than new concepts
Efficiency claims lack rigorous empirical support - provides GFLOPs comparisons but no wall-clock training/inference time comparisons, which are more practical metrics
Results are competitive but not state-of-the-art - 1.61 FID is respectable but doesn't substantially outperform existing methods, undermining the main value proposition
Detail preservation claims unvalidated - argues pixel-space better preserves fine details but provides only qualitative evidence without quantitative metrics
Incomplete comparisons - Table 1 mixes models with different sizes, parameter counts, and training epochs, making direct comparison difficult
Text-to-image results underspecified - PixelDiT-T2I training details (26M image-text pairs, preprocessing) lack clarity; no clear advantage over alternatives demonstrated
Missing practical considerations - no analysis of actual inference speed, memory usage during training/inference, or guidance on when practitioners should prefer this approach
Limited theoretical insight - paper doesn't provide principled explanation for why pixel-space modeling works well or what distinguishes this approach conceptually
Incomplete ablation analysis - limited investigation of why pixel pathway helps convergence; token compaction analysis relatively shallow
Brief limitations section - minimal discussion of failure cases, failure modes, or when approach would not be preferred

strengths: Technically sound dual-level architecture combining patch-level and pixel-level transformers with well-motivated design choices
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive comparisons to baselines, detailed ablations, and thorough reproducibility information in appendices
Achieves strong results within pixel-space modeling category (1.61 FID on ImageNet 256×256), demonstrating effective per-pixel modeling with AdaLN modulation
Addresses legitimate VAE artifact limitations by operating directly in pixel space, enabling cleaner detail preservation
Extends method to text-to-image generation with multi-modal DiT blocks and evaluates on multiple image editing tasks
weaknesses: Severe performance gap to latent-space baselines (1.61 vs 3.60 FID for LDM-4-G) undermines practical motivation; 'surpassing pixel models' claim only compares within inferior paradigm
Unclear computational efficiency justification; token compaction proposed but no direct latent-space comparison provided; ablation reveals memory fragility (OOM without compaction)
Limited technical novelty; dual-level architecture is straightforward, AdaLN modulation is existing technique, token compaction is engineering rather than fundamental contribution
Misleading comparative framing: overstates VAE reconstruction as fundamental problem while underplaying the quality trade-off inherent in pixel-space approach
Fails to answer critical question: when should practitioners use PixelDiT over established latent-space methods? No compelling use cases or practical advantages identified
Text-to-image results underwhelming (GenEval 0.74, DPG 83.5) despite architectural advantages; limited investigation of why benefits don't transfer from class-conditioned tasks
Narrow experimental scope limited to ImageNet 256×256; no evaluation on other benchmarks, higher resolutions, or scalability analysis where pixel-space efficiency would matter most
Acknowledged limitations inadequately addressed (Section G); sensitivity of CFG settings; convergence analysis suggests slower optimization for larger models
Quadratic memory/compute growth with resolution inherent to pixel-space severely limits scalability beyond 256×256, restricting practical applicability

strengths: Novel and well-motivated conceptual contribution challenging the latent-space diffusion paradigm by demonstrating competitive pixel-space performance
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple resolutions, metrics, and tasks with systematic ablation studies validating design choices
Elegant dual-level architecture (patch + pixel pathways) that balances computational efficiency with detail preservation through well-justified design decisions
Strong empirical results including competitive FID on ImageNet (1.61 at 256×256) and megapixel text-to-image generation with superior detail preservation for image editing
Excellent reproducibility with detailed architecture specifications, hyperparameters, training procedures, and implementation details enabling reproduction
Rigorous analysis including convergence studies by patch size, sampler comparisons, token compaction impact analysis, and depth allocation trade-off studies
Technical soundness with correct mathematical formulations and appropriate experimental methodology
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual components (pixel-wise AdaLN is straightforward AdaLN extension; pixel token compaction is learned token compression) despite novel combination

Insufficient computational trade-off analysis: while claiming efficiency, lacks wall-clock time and memory comparisons against latent-space baselines; unclear when practitioners should adopt pixel-space despite overhead
Text-to-image model limited to 1.3B parameters with acknowledged struggles on geometrically and textually complex objects; missing comparisons with recent 2024-2025 SOTA models

Incomplete guidance on when pixel-space is preferable: image editing benefits demonstrated qualitatively but not rigorously evaluated; no systematic comparison of detail preservation across image types

Limited generalization evaluation: restricted to natural images and faces with no assessment on specialized domains (medical, satellite imagery); unclear how architectural choices transfer across domains
Missing direct ablations (pixel-wise vs. global AdaLN, systematic removal of dual-level pathways) that could strengthen validation of individual components
Shallow treatment of limitations: brief limitations section with no systematic failure mode analysis beyond acknowledging model capacity constraints
Insufficient analysis of VAE artifact avoidance: claims lack rigorous quantitative validation and detailed comparison metrics

strengths: Well-motivated dual-level architecture that thoughtfully separates global semantic learning (patch-level) from local detail refinement (pixel-level) with sound design rationale
Strong competitive empirical results: 1.61 FID on ImageNet 256×256 (best for pixel-space models), scalable to 1024² resolution, and demonstrates practical quality advantages without VAE bottlenecks

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablation studies (Tables 5-6, Figures 5, 8, 10) systematically analyzing component contributions, solver choices, and architectural hyperparameters
Demonstrated practical advantage in image editing with superior detail preservation (0.00152 MSE vs. FLUX 0.009105 MSE) without VAE reconstruction artifacts, with thorough comparison in Table 14

Technically sound with correct mathematical formulations, detailed implementation specifications, and transparent discussion of limitations (Section I) including honest assessment of failure cases with complex objects
Eliminates autoencoder dependency, simplifying the generation pipeline and avoiding latent space distortion artifacts inherent in VAE-based approaches
weaknesses: Insufficient computational efficiency analysis: lacks wall-clock training/inference time comparisons and memory usage benchmarks versus latent diffusion models despite claiming efficiency; Table 6 GFLOPs provide limited practical context

Limited theoretical grounding for why pixel-space diffusion achieves comparable quality to latent approaches; dual-level design presented empirically without exploring alternative architectures or analyzing what semantic information pixel-level pathway captures

Narrow evaluation scope: primarily ImageNet and COCO Captions without domain generalization studies, human perceptual evaluation, or standard text-to-image benchmarks (missing CLIP-score comparisons); text-to-image limited to DPG-Bench and GenEval

Incremental novelty: individual components (patch-diffusion, AdaLN, token compression) are relatively standard; dual-level design, while effective, is a straightforward combination rather than introducing fundamental algorithmic insights

Training stability concerns acknowledged but not deeply analyzed: loss spikes for deeper architectures (M>4), velocity prediction instability requiring stabilization, suggesting practical deployment challenges not fully resolved

Multiple design choices lack sufficient justification: pixel-token compression mechanism (Eq. 7) appears arbitrary with 6 groups chosen empirically; choice of p=16 default acknowledges quality-speed tradeoff (Table 13 shows p=8 superior) without principled selection; complex AdaLN variants (Figure 3) with limited alternative exploration
Text-to-image results not clearly positioned as state-of-the-art (83.5 GenEval on DPG-Bench) with incomplete comparison to recent latent diffusion models (Flux, SD3)

Reproducibility challenges: dense design with many interconnected choices despite detailed appendices; code/models unavailable at review time; some critical preprocessing details relegated to appendix

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations across multiple resolutions and architectural variants, enabling reproducibility
Well-motivated dual-level architecture effectively addressing pixel-space computational complexity through thoughtful separation of patch-level semantics and pixel-level details
Competitive class-conditional image generation results (FID 1.61 on ImageNet 256) demonstrating pixel-space can match latent diffusion quality
Detailed technical reporting including architecture specifications, training configurations, and honest limitations discussion
Practical advantages in image editing applications with demonstrable background preservation benefits over VAE-based latent models
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primary contribution is engineering combination of existing techniques (patch-level DiT, AdaLN from prior work, standard token compression) rather than fundamental innovation
Text-to-image results substantially weaker than claimed (GenEval 0.78 vs SOTA 0.84+), contradicting central scalability claims and suggesting poor generalization to multi-modal conditioning
Inference speed (1.07 samples/sec on A100) is slower than latent methods, undermining efficiency claims; computational advantages appear limited to training phase only

Extensive architecture tuning and ablations (varying N, M depths, multiple training strategies) indicate brittle optimization requiring careful hyperparameter selection rather than robust method design

Insufficient practical justification for added complexity: VAE artifact avoidance provides only marginal visual improvements, image editing benefits are modest, and class-conditional quality matches existing latent models
Experimental setup inconsistencies with varying hyperparameters, non-standard preprocessing, and different training budgets across experiments complicate fair comparison of contributions
Scaling limitations revealed by degraded performance at 512² (FID 1.81 vs 1.61) and substantial further degradation at 1024² (GenEval 0.74), suggesting fundamental scaling challenges
Training stability concerns acknowledged (loss spikes in deeper architectures, instabilities during extended training) indicate potential robustness issues not adequately addressed
Text-to-image extension appears rushed with standard CLIP encoder and minimal architectural innovation; Table 4 results not meaningfully analyzed relative to latent baselines
Incomplete baseline comparisons: recent pixel-space methods (PixelFlow, U-ViT) not thoroughly analyzed; SOTA comparisons rely on published numbers rather than reproduced results

strengths: Novel dual-level transformer architecture elegantly addresses pixel-space modeling efficiency by separating patch-level semantic learning from pixel-level detail refinement
Comprehensive experimental validation with strong results (FID 1.61 on ImageNet 256×256 without autoencoder, outperforming pixel generative baselines) and rigorous ablation studies
Excellent reproducibility support including complete architectural specifications, implementation details, public code/models, and configuration tables for multiple model variants
Practical contributions demonstrated including training-free image editing without VAE artifacts and superior background preservation compared to latent-space models
Technically sound design with well-motivated pixel token compaction mechanism, dual-level AdaLN strategy, and clear mathematical formulation enabling reproducibility
Thorough appendix with detailed analysis of design choices, solver comparisons, empirical insights, and extensive qualitative results across diverse image categories
weaknesses: Computational efficiency gains not convincingly demonstrated; lacks clear FLOPs/memory comparison against similarly-sized latent-space models and inference speed benchmarks
Model capacity limitations acknowledged for complex geometries/textures; text-to-image at 1024² (GenEval 0.74, DPG 83.5) is competitive but not state-of-the-art
Training stability issues with velocity prediction loss spikes in deeper architectures remain an open challenge despite mitigation efforts
Limited novelty in individual components; main contribution is architectural combination of existing techniques (pixel diffusion, AdaLN) rather than fundamental innovation
Scalability to very high resolutions unclear; quadratic cost with resolution and no results beyond 1024² limit applicability to production systems requiring 2048²+ resolution
Modest incremental improvements in some benchmarks (FID 1.61 vs 1.81 vs PixelFlow-XL); different model sizes in comparisons complicate direct assessment of architectural contributions
